description:
We are a Cairo-registered multidisciplinary team interested in building practical, science-driven solutions for Earth and space. Our interests include AI/ML, software engineering, data analysis, and product development.

We welcome collaborators with strengths in physics or space science, scientific research, data science, UI/UX, and business/product development who enjoy turning complex questions into clear, testable prototypes.
summary: RotaNile is crop-rotation planning support for the Nile Delta. It uses NASA POWER daily climate data (meteorology from model output, solar radiation derived from satellites) and the MODIS MOD13Q1 version 061 vegetation index (NDVI) for five proposed Delta locations. Crop values come from an agronomy parameter base, and each value carries an evidence grade: verified, provisional or unresolved. The app ranks three-year rotations of wheat, berseem, cotton, maize and rice on water demand, soil health and climate risk, with priority weights the user sets. Each plan shows its evidence. NDVI is context only and does not enter any score. Data are the latest available at retrieval. RotaNile makes no forecast. Coordinates are proposed and have not been checked on imagery, climate values are grid-cell model output, and real-world validation was not performed.
details:
What it does

RotaNile compares three-year crop rotations for the Nile Delta. The user picks one of five proposed Delta locations and sets priorities for water, soil health and climate risk. Limits on crops, salinity and the water cap are optional. The app ranks rotations of wheat, berseem, cotton, maize and rice and shows what drives each rank. Ranked plans download as CSV or JSON.

How it works

For each location the app reads daily NASA POWER data: meteorology from model output and satellite-derived solar radiation. Reference evapotranspiration follows the FAO-56 Penman-Monteith method, and crop water demand comes from crop coefficients by growth stage. The soil health index combines four proxies: legume nitrogen input, repetition pressure, salinity exposure and crop diversity. The climate risk index has heat and water components. The engine normalizes each score (min-max), weights it by the user's priorities and ranks the plans. It also flags plans that no other plan beats on every criterion (Pareto dominance). MODIS MOD13Q1 version 061 NDVI is shown as context only and enters no score.

Evidence and labels

The agronomy configuration holds 113 graded parameters: 49 verified, 56 provisional and 8 unresolved. Twenty-five of the provisional values were recalled from the literature and not read in an opened source, and the configuration says so. Each plan shows the evidence behind it. The interface labels data as modeled, satellite-derived or observed, and shows the data end date as latest available at retrieval.

Intended impact

RotaNile is planning support. It lets a user compare options and see which assumptions drive a ranking. It makes no forecast and gives no price or income figures.

Tools

TypeScript, React 19, TanStack Start, Router and Query, Vite, Tailwind CSS 4, zod, Vitest, ESLint and Prettier, run with Bun. The engine runs in a web worker. Data come from NASA POWER and the ORNL DAAC MODIS web service. A frozen snapshot keeps the demo independent of service speed. Fonts are Michroma and Public Sans.

What we considered

Coordinates are proposed and were not checked on imagery. Climate values are grid-cell model output. NDVI pixels are 250 m and can mix land covers. The third "nili" season and capillary rise are not modeled. The climate source changes within the 2020-to-present period, and we did not assess consistency across that change. No outside review took place, and real-world validation was not performed.
